OpenCode Skills Not Loading? Check the File, ID and Scope

Run opencode --version, then check for .opencode/skills/<id>/SKILL.md in the workspace you opened. In V1, list discovered skills from that workspace with opencode debug skill --pure. In V2, use the ID from the file path and check whether the selected agent can load it.

  1. Install a minimal skill and check discovery
  2. Listed but not used: check loading and permissions
  3. Wrong content: find the winning copy
  4. What the V1 discovery test showed

How is your OpenCode skill failing?

See stepsSee stepsSee steps

Install a minimal skill and check discovery

From the repository root, create .opencode/skills/ipunk-skill-check/SKILL.md with the following contents. Use a new ID if that name already exists. For this folder-based skill, keep the filename uppercase.

---
name: ipunk-skill-check
description: Return a marker when asked to test skill loading
---

When asked for the skill marker, reply with PROJECT_SKILL_FIXTURE.
Do not call tools or edit files.
  1. In V1, run opencode debug skill --pure and find ipunk-skill-check. The recorded path should point to your workspace. A zero exit status alone does not show that your skill was found. This command may print skill content; keep private output local.
  2. In V2, use the exact path-derived ID ipunk-skill-check and mention it as @ipunk-skill-check. The YAML name is a display label in V2. For a folder-based skill, do not substitute a differently named Markdown file for SKILL.md.
  3. If uncertain where the app is looking, reopen the intended repo and try the minimal project-local file before adding global copies. If the minimal file works, compare the original path and frontmatter with the example.

Listed but not used: check loading and permissions

In V1, ask the agent to use the named skill and return its marker. Inspect the transcript for a successful skill call. Add a nonempty description even if the V1 CLI listed the entry without one. Check the selected agent’s permission.skill rules for the skill name.

In V2, the description makes the skill discoverable to the model, and opencode/autoinvoke: false excludes it from automatic discovery. Try the explicit @ipunk-skill-check mention and verify it resolves. Check the selected agent’s skill permission for that exact ID; the last matching rule wins. Keep intentional denials in place and ask the owner if you need access.

A marker in a reply by itself is weak proof. Check the tool result or resolved skill attachment, and avoid putting the marker value in the prompt.

Wrong content: find the winning copy

In V1, read location and the authored marker in the debug output. In the test below, a project copy won over one global copy. Check the path in your own run before moving either copy. In V2, check for duplicate IDs in global, project, and explicitly configured sources: a later source can override the project entry.

To keep both definitions, give one a unique lowercase ID and use the new ID when loading it. In V1, also update the YAML name to match its directory. Rerun the discovery or explicit load check and confirm the expected file or marker.

What the V1 discovery test showed

  • Valid file: the project fixture appeared.
  • Wrong filename: guide.md in the skill folder did not appear.
  • Missing description: the fixture appeared without a description. This was a CLI listing, not proof the agent could discover or load it.
  • Duplicate global and project: the returned path and marker were from the project.

Tested on macOS arm64 with OpenCode 1.19.6 on Nov 24, 2026, in isolated Git workspaces without model calls. See the recorded fixture output. V2 procedures are based on documentation and were not run in this fixture.

Sources: V1 agent skills · V2 skills. For broader configuration, see the OpenCode permission setup.
